comparator.name: History
comparator.sourceNotes: Groningen begins with a chronological survey, then develops political, cultural, social and economic history through research seminars. The redesigned final year shown here combines a minor, an interdisciplinary choice, regional public history and a thesis.
components: A Global History of the Netherlands
History II: The Making of the Modern World, 1500–1945
IMPACT course: Global Changes or Cultural Heritage
Choose one 10 EC course in Global Change or Cultural Heritage.
The programme reserves a semester for a 30 EC minor.
Choose one course in Cultural Heritage, Global Change, Humane AI and the Digital Society, or Stories We Live By.
Regions III: Specialization and Public History
Study a region in depth and learn to communicate historical research to the public. Complete the first year before taking this course.
The regulations require completion of years one and two before the thesis.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Regional and global history from the ancient world through the present, including Dutch history in global context
Connections between the historical past and present political, social and cultural questions
Political, cultural, economic and social history as explicit disciplinary directions
Historical evidence, source criticism, methods, historiography, theory, interpretation and debate
Regional research, historical writing and independent thesis research
Public history, cultural heritage and communicating historical change beyond the university
adjacent: Political culture, international order, conflict and institutions in historical perspective
Economic and social history, inequality, organisations and long-run change
Cultural history, identity, representation, heritage and public memory
Global change as an interdisciplinary history theme
questions: How do historical developments connect the past to present political, social, economic and cultural questions?
How can historical sources and interpretations be analysed critically and used as evidence?
How have regions, empires, institutions, conflict, inequality and cultural identities changed across periods?

selection.assessment: Three directions combine a shared history sequence with separate emphases in cultural interpretation, politics and conflict, or economy and society. Groningen provides a more continuous disciplinary sequence from antiquity through the present.

alternatives.label: History, culture & public memory
alternatives.labelReason: The option combines historical inquiry with the study of objects, images, museums and documentary media.
alternatives.concept: Study how people interpret and share the past. Build from modern history, art and archaeology to Indigenous histories, museums, film and documentary work.
progression: Modern History and art history introduce chronological and visual analysis. Later courses use archives, objects, oral accounts and documentary media to investigate and communicate the past.

alternatives.label: History, politics & conflict
alternatives.labelReason: The option adds comparative politics, international relations and law to the history of empire, warfare and colonialism.
alternatives.concept: Study how empires, institutions and conflict shape societies. Combine historical sources with comparative politics, international relations and law to explore power and its consequences.
alternatives.distinctness: Differs from History, culture & public memory by 82.5 EC each way. It emphasises political institutions, international law and conflict.
progression: Historical and legal foundations prepare for later work in empire, conflict, international law and European institutions. The history seminar develops a sustained source-based argument.

alternatives.label: History, economy & society
alternatives.labelReason: Historical study of social change is combined with economic reasoning, social theory and qualitative and quantitative methods.
alternatives.concept: Study how economic change and social institutions shape people’s lives. Combine history and sociology with economics, policy analysis and quantitative research.
alternatives.distinctness: Differs from History, culture & public memory by 82.5 EC and from History, politics & conflict by 60 EC each way. It emphasises economic change, inequality and policy.
progression: Introduction to Economics and Research Methods & Statistics prepare for macroeconomics, public economics, behavioural economics and econometrics. Policy analysis applies this preparation to a concrete case.

blocks: Historical periods, comparison & regional and global coverage
Both study ancient societies. UCR focuses on archaeology and material culture.
Groningen surveys the Middle Ages in a dedicated course. UCR studies parts of the period through empire, war and art.
UCR studies Renaissance art, trade and exchange in the Mediterranean, one part of Groningen’s broader survey.
Both survey major political, economic and social changes of the twentieth century. UCR begins its survey in 1815.
Both examine historical power and political organisation. UCR compares empires across periods and regions.
Historical methods, data, writing & independent inquiry
Groningen studies Dutch history in a global context in a dedicated course.
Groningen introduces the methods of historical research before students start the thematic seminars.
Groningen requires a research seminar in social and economic history. UCR combines history, economics and sociology across several courses.
Both examine how scholars interpret the past. UCR focuses on the history of art history.
Groningen requires a 10 EC thesis. UCR’s American Century course develops historical research through a course paper, and optional independent research sits outside the illustrated schedules.
Both develop regional historical inquiry and public communication. UCR works with Indigenous histories and multimedia.

notes.text: Groningen teaches a continuous History curriculum from antiquity through the present, including dedicated seminars, regional research and a required thesis. The UCR options combine history with courses in culture, politics or economics and society. Their period coverage and research requirements differ.

audience.programmeDescription: Groningen History studies the past from antiquity to the present. Students learn to interpret sources, study regions and communicate historical research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options explore historical questions through culture and memory, politics and conflict, or economy and society. Groningen follows a continuous History curriculum and requires a thesis.
